1.title: Asset and Vulnerability Management
1.text: Welcome to Module thirteen: Asset and Vulnerability Management. It covers the exam area Security Operations. Each part of this module comes from the study notes of the same name, so you can read the notes after you watch.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do three things. four point two Explain the security implications of proper hardware, software, and data asset management. four point three Given a scenario, perform tasks associated with vulnerability management. Practice with exam-style questions and a recall check.

1.title: Where This Fits in the Exam
1.text: Here is where this module sits in the exam. Exam area: Security Operations (twenty-seven percent). Exam format: up to ninety questions in ninety minutes; a score of seven hundred fifty on a scale of one hundred to nine hundred passes. Validated against: the official Comp T I A Security plus S Y zero eight oh one V eight exam objectives.

1.title: Asset management
1.text: Asset management. You cannot protect what you do not know you have. Asset management tracks hardware, software and data through their whole life. Planning or scoping. What happens: Decide what is needed and the requirements. Security point: Include security requirements early. Acquisition or procurement. What happens: Buy from trusted suppliers. Security point: Check supply chain risk. Assignment or accounting. What happens: Record an owner and a record for each asset. Security point: Accountability, inventory.

1.title: Asset management, continued
1.text: Asset management. Monitoring or asset tracking. What happens: Track location, state and use. Security point: Find unmanaged and rogue assets. Disposal or decommissioning. What happens: Retire safely. Security point: Sanitize data, remove from inventory, certify destruction.

1.title: Asset management, continued
1.text: Asset management. The figure shows this: The asset life cycle from planning to disposal, with a security action at each stage. Exam tip: An accurate inventory is the first step of security. Disposal needs data sanitization (wiping, destruction) and removal from the inventory. Ownership gives accountability.

1.title: Vulnerability management: identification
1.text: Vulnerability management: identification. Scanning. Automated vulnerability scanners check systems for known flaws (credentialed scans log in and see more; non-credentialed scans see what an outsider sees). I P A M. Internet Protocol Address Management: tracks I P space and finds unknown devices. C S P M (cloud security posture management). Cloud security posture management: checks cloud configuration for risks. Source code review. Examine code (manually or with static analysis) for flaws.

1.title: Prioritization, remediation, verification and reporting
1.text: Prioritization, remediation, verification and reporting. Prioritization. Severity assessment (C V S S, exploitability, asset value, exposure) and penetration test report review. Remediation. Patch, change configuration, compensating control, or accept the risk (documented). Verification. Rescan or retest to confirm the fix worked. Reporting. Internal reports to owners and management; external reports to others.

1.title: External reporting
1.text: External reporting. Bounty program. Pays researchers who report flaws. Responsible disclosure policy. Rules for reporting a flaw and giving the vendor time to fix before going public. Exam tip: The first step of security is knowing your assets: an unmanaged device is an unpatched and unmonitored device.

1.title: External reporting, continued
1.text: External reporting. The figure shows this: The vulnerability management loop: identify, prioritize, remediate, verify, report. Exam tip: The loop is identify, prioritize, remediate, verify, report and then repeat. A false positive is a finding that is not real; a false negative is a missed real flaw. Credentialed scans find more than non-credentialed ones.

1.title: Practice Question 1
1.text: Question one. Fabrikam Outdoors retires old laptops. What must happen before they are recycled? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: Data is sanitized and the assets are removed from inventory. Disposal requires secure sanitization or destruction of data and updating the inventory.

1.title: Practice Question 2
1.text: Question two. A scan that signs in to servers with an administrator account finds more issues than an external scan. Why? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: It is a credentialed scan with deeper visibility. Credentialed scans can inspect configuration and installed software that outsiders cannot see.

1.title: Practice Question 3
1.text: Question three. A team fixes a flaw and then runs the scanner again to prove it is gone. Which step is this? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: Verification. Rescanning confirms that remediation worked.

1.title: Practice Question 4
1.text: Question four. A company pays outside researchers who report security flaws in its public services. What is this program? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: Bounty program. A bounty program rewards responsible reports of vulnerabilities.

1.title: Practice Question 5
1.text: Question five. Which tool checks cloud account settings for risky configurations such as open storage? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: C S P M. Cloud security posture management evaluates cloud configuration against best practices.

1.title: Practice Question 6
1.text: Question six. A scanner reports a critical flaw that does not exist on the target. What is this finding? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: False positive. A reported issue that is not real is a false positive.

1.title: Recall Check 1
1.text: Recall check one. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question one. Name the five stages of the asset life cycle in the objectives. Answer: Planning or scoping, acquisition or procurement, assignment or accounting, monitoring or tracking, and disposal or decommissioning. Question two. What is the loop of vulnerability management? Answer: Identify, prioritize, remediate, verify and report. Question three. What does I P A M do? Answer: Tracks I P address space and helps find unknown devices.

1.title: Recall Check 2
1.text: Recall check two. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question four. What is responsible disclosure? Answer: Reporting a flaw privately and giving the vendor time to fix it. Question five. What is a false negative? Answer: A real vulnerability that the scan missed. Question six. Name two remediation options. Answer: Patching and a compensating control (or documented acceptance).

1.title: Module Recap
1.text: Here is the recap. Asset life cycle: plan, acquire, assign (owner), monitor and track, dispose (sanitize, update inventory). Identify: scanning (credentialed deeper), I P A M, C S P M, source code review. Prioritize and fix: severity, exposure, asset value, pen test reports; patch, change configuration, compensate or accept. Verify and report: rescan; internal and external reports; bounty programs; responsible disclosure. In the next module, we continue the course.
